name: Wipro (Elite NTH & Turbo)
tagline: Elite National Talent Hunt: aptitude, essay and coding in one sitting

overview.about: Wipro's main fresher route is the Elite National Talent Hunt (NTH) for engineering graduates, leading to the Project Engineer role. Strong performers may be considered for the higher-paying Turbo role, which involves a tougher assessment and interview. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.
eligibility: B.E./B.Tech (and M.E./M.Tech in some cycles) from the batches named in the notice
Typically 60% or more in 10th, 12th and graduation (as reported)
Full-time courses only; at most one active backlog at test time, cleared before joining (check notice)

pattern.note: Choose Java, C, C++ or Python

overview.frequency: Elite NTH runs once or twice a year; campus drives in season

cards.title: Tight timing
cards.body: About 52 questions in under 50 minutes across three sub-sections — roughly a minute per question. Percentile-style sectional cut-offs are reported. Pattern as reported for 2025–26 drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Quant topics
points: Number system, LCM/HCF
Percentages, profit, interest
Time-work, speed, ratios
Probability, P&C, mensuration

cards.title: Logical & verbal topics
points: Series, coding-decoding, directions, blood relations
Syllogisms, seating, data sufficiency
Synonyms/antonyms, sentence correction, RC

cards.title: Essay round
cards.body: You get one topic and ~20 minutes for ~200–300 words. Graded on grammar, structure and clarity, not opinion.

cards.title: Essay skeleton
cards.body: Intro (2 lines: define topic + your stance) → 2 body paragraphs (one point + example each) → conclusion (restate + forward-looking line). Example topic: 'Is AI a threat to jobs?'

cards.title: Essay hygiene
cards.body: Short sentences, no slang or SMS language, consistent tense, paragraph breaks. Leave 2 minutes to proofread spellings and articles.

cards.q: Which essay structure is safest in a 20-minute test?
cards.explain: A clear structure is easy to grade and to finish in time.

notes.p:
Wipro's fresher hiring for roles such as **Project Engineer** runs through the **Elite National Talent Hunt (NTH)**. The online assessment is reported to include an **aptitude test** (logical reasoning, quantitative ability, verbal ability), a **written communication test (essay)** and an **online programming test**, followed by interviews. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

The aptitude section has many questions in limited time; sectional cut-offs are common, so balance your effort across all three parts.

**Quant.** A 240 m train passes a pole in 24 s. How long to pass a 650 m platform? Speed = 10 m/s; distance = 890 m → **89 s**.

**Quant.** A sum doubles in 5 years at simple interest. Rate? 100/5 = **20%** per year.

**Logical.** Odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125 → **100** (others are cubes).

**Logical.** If FRIEND is coded as HUMJTK, how is CANDLE coded? The shifts are +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7: C+2 = E, A+3 = D, N+4 = R, D+5 = I, L+6 = R, E+7 = L → **EDRIRL**.

**Verbal.** Choose the correct sentence: 'Neither of the answers are correct' vs 'Neither of the answers is correct' → **is** (neither is singular).

The written communication test gives a topic and a short time (around 20 minutes is commonly reported) to write roughly **200–300 words**. It is often checked by software for grammar, spelling, structure and relevance, and then by people. Clear, simple, error-free English scores better than fancy vocabulary.

**Template:** (1) **Introduction** — one or two sentences that state your position. (2) **Body paragraph 1** — first reason with an example. (3) **Body paragraph 2** — second reason or the other side with an example. (4) **Conclusion** — restate the position and suggest a way forward.

**Sample outline — 'Is technology making us less social?'** Intro: technology changes how we connect rather than simply reducing it. Body 1: video calls keep families in different cities close. Body 2: endless scrolling can replace face-to-face time, especially for teenagers. Conclusion: use technology with limits — device-free meals, scheduled meet-ups.

points: Going off-topic or writing a story instead of an argument.
One giant paragraph with no structure.
SMS language, slang or overused phrases like 'in today's modern world'.
Spelling mistakes from typing fast — keep 2 minutes to proofread.
Writing far below the word limit.

notes.p: How to use your time in the aptitude test:
points: Start with the section you are strongest in to build confidence, if the test allows choosing order.
Quant: target formula-based questions (percentages, TSD, time-work) first.
Logical: series and coding-decoding are quick wins; leave long puzzles for last.
Verbal: grammar and vocabulary questions take seconds; read RC questions before the passage.
Never leave the essay box short — write a complete structure even if simple.
Aptitude: logical, quant, verbal with sectional cut-offs.
Essay: intro, two body paragraphs, conclusion.
Aim for 200–300 words of clear, correct English.
Use examples in every body paragraph.
Proofread before submitting.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

cards.title: Coding format
cards.body: Two problems in about 60 minutes, usually one easier and one harder. Choose C, C++, Java or Python. Hidden test cases decide the score.

cards.title: Common problem types
points: Array manipulation and searching
String processing (vowels, words, palindromes)
Number logic (primes, Armstrong, digit sums)
Pattern printing occasionally

cards.title: Example: Armstrong number
Turbo
cards.body: Wipro Turbo is a higher-pay fresher role. Selection uses a tougher coding/technical assessment and interview; strong NTH performers may be considered. Check the current notice for how to qualify.

cards.title: Interviews
cards.body: Technical: project, OOP, DBMS, a simple program, maybe a puzzle. HR: relocation, shift flexibility, service agreement, why Wipro.

cards.title: Edge cases
cards.body: Test negative numbers, zero, a single element and the largest constraint before submitting — hidden cases target exactly these.

cards.q: Before submitting a coding solution, which check helps most with hidden test cases?
options: Run edge inputs like 0, negatives and max size
cards.explain: Edge cases are where most hidden test failures happen.

notes.p: Wipro's online programming test is reported to give **two problems in about an hour**, solved in languages like C, C++, Java or Python, judged on hidden test cases. Questions are usually easy to medium: number manipulation, strings, arrays and simple patterns. Some drives also run **Wipro Turbo** (a higher-package track) with tougher coding and interviews for top performers. Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.

**Problem.** Read a positive integer and repeatedly add its digits until a single digit remains.

`n = int(input())
while n >= 10:
    n = sum(int(d) for d in str(n))
print(n)`

Sample input:
`9875`

Output:
`2`

9 + 8 + 7 + 5 = 29 → 2 + 9 = 11 → 1 + 1 = 2. A faster O(1) formula exists: for n > 0 the answer is 1 + (n − 1) mod 9, which you can mention in the interview.

notes.h: Sample problem 2: Armstrong numbers in a range
notes.p:
**Problem.** Print all Armstrong numbers between A and B (a number equal to the sum of its digits each raised to the power of the number of digits).

`a, b = map(int, input().split())
res = []
for n in range(a, b + 1):
    digits = str(n)
    if n == sum(pow(int(d), len(digits)) for d in digits):
        res.append(n)
print(*res)`

Sample input:
`100 999`

Output:
`153 370 371 407`

Time is O((B − A) × d) where d is the digit count. Handle the case of no results as the problem states (for example, print -1).

**Q: Explain your project and your exact role.** A: Two-minute summary: problem, stack, your module, a challenge, the result.

**Q: What is the difference between an array and a linked list?** A: Arrays give O(1) indexed access with contiguous memory; linked lists give O(1) insert/delete at a known node but O(n) access.

**Q: What is a primary key and a foreign key?** A: A primary key uniquely identifies rows; a foreign key references a primary key in another table.

**Q: Why Wipro?** A: Mention its training for freshers, its range of client domains, and your fit — with one specific fact you looked up.

**Q: Are you open to any technology and location?** A: Show flexibility honestly; freshers are often assigned based on business needs.
Common mistakes in the coding round:
points: Printing extra text or spaces around the answer.
Not handling the empty or 'no result' case.
Integer overflow in C/Java for large inputs.
Wasting time perfecting code style instead of passing test cases.
Two coding problems, roughly an hour (as reported).
Focus on numbers, strings and arrays.
Check edge cases and exact output format.
Interview: project, DSA basics, DBMS, OOP, HR.
Turbo track: harder coding, higher package.
Pattern as reported for recent drives; confirm on the official careers page.
